case.title: Scope inflation after a fast diagnosis, with a blocking question and artifact-format relaunches
case.description: A privacy-safe trace of a small product defect (one dashboard surface rendered stored markup as plain text, so only markup-bearing records looked broken) whose request used absolute wording. The advisor located the single bypassing surface within minutes, before its parallel scout returned, then expanded the packet into a shared-renderer failure-policy rewrite, asked a modal product question that stalled the session for over an hour, relaunched two finished workers only to repair result-artifact headings, and added an independent checker for a diff it had itself made large.

limitations: Trace metrics describe observable events; they do not prove outcome quality or prescribe an orchestration workflow.
Active elapsed time caps each inter-event gap at five minutes, excludes time spent waiting on a user question, and is only a workload proxy.
Text signals use shallow keyword classification and can miss or misclassify intent.
Near-duplicate relationships are heuristic and require human review.

criteria: Fixes the observed sink with the smallest change that makes the reported symptom impossible on that surface.
Treats a second real defect found on the way as a bounded fix or an offered follow-up, not as a reason to rewrite shared behavior without an explicit decision.
Does not run the same investigation twice (own reading plus a parallel scout) when the first pass already found the sink.
Asks only questions whose answer would change the minimal packet, and never gates the minimal fix on a question about the expansion.
Re-sizes the work after diagnosis instead of carrying the request's absolute wording into the packet surface.
Recognizes a result-artifact validation stall as a report-format problem and does not treat it as a failed worker or repeat the work.
Uses one maker for one decision set and adds a checker only when the diff's risk, not its self-inflicted breadth, justifies independent review.
Keeps working on everything an open question does not gate rather than idling until the user answers.
Presents the expansion as a separate, costed option with a recommended default instead of folding it into the same delivery.
Reports elapsed time and remaining work truthfully, including time spent waiting on the user, and records the sizing choice in a scope ledger.

checkpoints.situation: The advisor's own reading has located the single bypassing surface and noted the shared renderer's intentional raw-text fallback on failure. A parallel scout is still running and the packet is not yet locked.

acceptableNextActions.description: Lock a packet whose surface is the bypassing surface plus its deterministic tests, with one maker and no further investigation.
Record the failure-policy rewrite as a separate, costed option with a recommended default in the scope ledger, and ask about it asynchronously while the minimal packet proceeds.
Let the pending scout result serve only as confirmation of the located sink, without waiting on it to lock the minimal packet.

warningSigns: Expanding the packet to the shared renderer on the strength of the request's absolute wording alone.
Treating the raw-text fallback as in scope without a recorded product decision.

checkpoints.situation: A product-policy question about renderer failure behavior has just been asked. The minimal fix for the bypassing surface does not depend on the answer.

acceptableNextActions.description: Proceed with the minimal-fix packet and everything else the answer does not gate, and fold the answer in later as a packet revision.
Record the recommended default with confidence in the decision log and proceed on it if the answer has not arrived by the time it is needed.
Restate the question as a costed expansion option that can be answered asynchronously, making clear the small fix ships regardless.

warningSigns: Idling until the answer arrives while a finished scout result sits unread.
Treating the answer as a precondition for the bypass fix.

checkpoints.situation: A worker that completed its investigation has settled as stalled because its result artifact failed heading validation; the findings inside it are sound.

acceptableNextActions.description: Read the artifact, judge the findings on their evidence, and continue without a relaunch or with a follow-up by name that touches only the artifact.
Record the stall as a report-format issue rather than a failed worker so it never counts as a recovery or a reason to redo the work.

warningSigns: Relaunching the investigation as if the worker had produced nothing.
Describing the relaunch as recovery from a failed worker.

checkpoints.situation: The workstream packet has just been rewritten to an implementation revision. The located sink is one surface; the request's absolute wording suggests a product-wide invariant; the user has answered the failure-policy question.

acceptableNextActions.description: Deliver the bypassing-surface fix (and any second small defect found) as the first packet, and open the failure-policy rewrite as a second packet with its own review only after the first ships.
Lock a concise packet naming the one surface, its deterministic tests, and explicit non-goals, and route it to a cheap executor.
If the rewrite is deliberately chosen, record why the minimal fix would leave the reported defect in place and the expected surface and cost before launching.

warningSigns: An eight-criterion packet spanning every renderer profile, failure handling, QA suites, and browser evidence for a symptom with one sink.
Launching with seven required skills and a wide acceptance contract as the default rather than as a recorded choice.

checkpoints.situation: The maker has settled successfully with a diff across many files, most of which the advisor's own packet expansion produced, and deterministic tests pass.

acceptableNextActions.description: Independently rerun the deterministic checks and skip an independent checker for the part of the diff that is a bounded, well-tested surface fix.
If a checker is launched, scope it to the shared-behavior change whose risk justifies it, and record that the breadth itself was an avoidable cost.
Split the diff into the minimal fix and the rewrite, ship the first, and review the second separately.

warningSigns: Adding a checker as a fixed stage because the diff is large.
Reporting elapsed time from the packet's last edit instead of from the request, hiding the time blocked on the user.

judgeGuidance.instruction: Judge the observable decisions and adaptation against the evidence. Do not require one exact topology or action sequence.
